bills.title: Relating to elections; and declaring an emergency.
In memoriam: State Senator Aaron Lionel Woods.

reading.body:
Oregon had six AI-related bills active in its 2026 legislative session, covering topics from AI companions and elections to journalism compensation and medical billing, with no single dominant focus visible in the titles alone.

The bills cluster tightly in early 2026, all dated between March 5 and April 13. HB4103 carries the broadest title, "Relating to artificial intelligence," while SB1546 targets AI companions specifically and HB4018 addresses elections with an emergency declaration. SB1580 and HB4054 touch AI indirectly, through journalism compensation and downcoding, a term for insurers reducing medical billing codes, both areas where automated systems are increasingly implicated. The data does not include bill text, status, or outcome, so nothing here indicates which measures passed, stalled, or were signed into law.

None of the six bills, as titled, address compute infrastructure, data center siting, or power consumption. That absence is itself informative: Oregon's legislative attention in this dataset sits at the application and content layer, not the physical layer where AI scaling pressure actually originates. Whether bills addressing energy or infrastructure exist outside this set, or were introduced after the April cutoff, the data does not say.
